key_observations.source_locator: Cas1-Cas2 complex formation is required in vivo; Fig. 3 and supplementary stability comparison
key_observations.observation: Cas2 C-terminal beta6-beta7 deletion prevents detectable acquisition and stable co-precipitation with Cas1. Cas1 R252E similarly loses stable complex formation and acquisition, while purified R252E retains the expected Cas1-dimer gel-filtration behavior. Single Cas2 E65R is tolerated; E65R/D84R double substitution abolishes acquisition. Tolerated Cas1-tail deletion and Cas2 E65R retain complex formation.
key_observations.limit: A deletion can affect more than one local contact. The study does not provide a complete independent folding/stability assay for every Cas2 variant, so these are not all proven interface-only perturbations.

key_observations.source_locator: The catalytic activity of Cas2 is dispensable in vivo; Fig. 4c-d,g-h
key_observations.observation: E. coli Cas2 E9A and E9R support PCR-detected spacer acquisition at levels described as similar to wild type; E9 mutation also retains complex formation and lysate CRISPR-bait recognition. Cas2 R14A retains acquisition, whereas interface-associated R18A has low acquisition. Cas1 conserved active-site alanine substitutions abolish acquisition.
key_observations.limit: The directly measured result is acquisition/assembly/bait behavior of E. coli mutants. The loss-of-nuclease expectation relies on the conserved-site interpretation and earlier other-species assays; no direct E. coli E9-mutant nuclease-null assay is demonstrated by this reading. No new quantitative frequency or statistical equivalence was calculated here.

key_observations.source_locator: Protospacer DNA integration by Cas1-Cas2; Fig. 1 and Extended Data Figs. 2-3
key_observations.observation: Purified Cas1/Cas2 joins labelled protospacers covalently to plasmid DNA. Cas1 H208A and D221A are defective; Cas2 E9Q supports integration. Cas2 beta6-beta7 deletion fails to support the reaction. Cas1 alone gives low integration with Mn2+, and Cas2 substantially enhances integration.
key_observations.limit: Cas2 is required for efficient tested complex behavior, not for every detectable Cas1 strand-transfer event under all conditions. These integration assays do not demonstrate every stage of immune protection or protospacer generation.

key_observations.source_locator: Integration and disintegration products; Integration requires 3-prime-OH protospacer ends
key_observations.observation: Radiolabel incorporation and product analysis distinguish integration products from plasmid topoisomers. Band X is not radiolabelled and is interpreted through disintegration/topology experiments. Blocking both protospacer 3-prime hydroxyls prevents integration; Cas1 also catalyses disintegration of a defined half-site substrate.
key_observations.limit: A change in plasmid migration is not automatically covalent spacer integration. Cas1's demonstrated integrase strand-transfer role must not be collapsed into an unsupported requirement that Cas1 or Cas2 cuts donor DNA to generate all prespacers.

key_observations.source_locator: The Cas1-Cas2 complex is essential for CRISPR locus binding
key_observations.observation: Purified complexes were not sequence-specific in the tested EMSA. In lysate CRISPR-target-bait precipitation, Cas1 preference depends on Cas2 and a compatible complex, although Cas2 itself is not detected in washed eluates.
key_observations.limit: No Cas2 in a washed target-bait eluate does not establish absence of all direct Cas2-DNA contacts. This is target-locus DNA in lysate, distinct from the donor protospacer captured in the later structure.

key_observations.observation: A four-Cas1/two-Cas2 complex positions the central donor duplex over Cas2 and terminal donor 3-prime ends in two Cas1 sites. Cas2 R16/R78 are part of a phosphate-backbone clamp; R16E and R78E strongly reduce in vivo acquisition, whereas R77E is tolerated. Cas1 clamp/channel and end-splaying mutants supply additional functional comparisons.
key_observations.limit: Contact presence alone does not establish functional necessity: R77 is an explicit tolerated contact-site example. Not every Cas2 contact mutant was directly assayed for binding affinity in isolation.

key_observations.method: Biopython 1.88 reads model 1, author chain/residue numbering. Euclidean nearest-heavy-atom comparisons within deposited assembly-1 atoms; no added symmetry mates. Polar groups are Glu OE1/OE2, Asp OD1/OD2 and Arg NE/NH1/NH2. DNA phosphate targets are OP1/OP2. Full atom-pair records and file hashes are saved.
actual_results: Across both Cas2 copies and both structures, R16 terminal-polar-group to DNA phosphate oxygen minima are 2.490-2.879 A; R78 minima are 2.378-3.017 A.

Cas2 R18 side-chain to Cas1 minima are 2.726-3.070 A, consistently at the Cas1 backbone near residue 4. The E9 side-chain to Cas1 minima are 13.834-14.602 A, spatially separating the signature acidic site from this direct inter-protein contact in these models.
The two donor terminal O3-prime atoms lie 2.879-3.558 A from H208 NE2 in Cas1 chains A/C. Cas2 E9 carboxylate-to-nearest donor terminal O3-prime distances are 47.547-50.240 A.

E9 is not simply remote from every DNA atom: all-side-chain nearest-DNA distances range from 3.902 to 4.213 A, and terminal-carboxylate to phosphate-oxygen minima range from 4.511 to 5.822 A. Geometry therefore cannot be used as a proof of no DNA interaction or no nuclease chemistry.
key_observations.changed_inference: The deposited models support spatially distinct contributions: a Cas2 central donor-DNA surface and Cas1-assembly interface versus Cas1 integration-end positioning. This is a positive structural explanation compatible with the functional mutant results, rather than inferring a scaffold solely from a catalytic-site mutant that still works.
key_observations.limits: Static 2.951/3.2-A models, approximate distances, no energetic or hydrogen-bond inference, no density/refinement analysis, no binding measurement, no mutant structural simulation and no independent proof that E9 is catalytically inactive. The two structures are related preparations from one study, not independent biological replications.

modularity_test.existing_pattern_under_test: F01/F03 contributor-attribution pattern requested by parent; no new category or lane is proposed
modularity_test.parent_scientific_question: What does Cas2 contribute to spacer acquisition in the specified system? This is the scoped job, not a thought-pattern value.
modularity_test.reused_thought: Keep the system's measured acquisition/integration output; distinguish catalytic, assembly and substrate-positioning contributions, and revise only the contribution contradicted by the selective evidence.
child_choices_this_constrains: Select a Cas2 signature-site versus assembly-interface contrast rather than infer two catalytic requirements from two nuclease names.
Seek a defined integration product and Cas1/Cas2 mutant comparison rather than call any plasmid mobility change integration.
Seek positive Cas2 substrate/assembly evidence rather than conclude an inert scaffold solely from E9 tolerance.
Withhold a nuclease-null claim when the direct protein/assay-specific catalytic-loss validation is missing.
modularity_test.experimental_layout_not_thought_unit: Point substitutions, truncation, co-immunoprecipitation, PCR, purified integration and crystallography are author experimental layouts/operations. No wet lab was available here. Our tools retrieved their records and made descriptive coordinate calculations.
modularity_test.ordinary_metadata_not_thought_unit: Donor species, recipient strain, metal condition, protein construct, DNA substrate, numbering and deposited model identity must travel with the observation; these are not selectable reasoning patterns.
modularity_test.analogy_supported: Like the earlier coupled-reaction/activator cases, a real system endpoint cannot be assigned to every participating protein as the same catalytic contribution. Selectively retained activity distinguishes required participation from requirement for one proposed chemistry. The same inference can guide a source inquiry outside metabolic enzymes.
where_analogy_breaks: Cas2 is not being assigned a replacement metabolic reaction or a consumed-substrate-supply role. Its supported contribution concerns complex assembly and donor-DNA geometry.

Cas1 catalysis is integrase strand transfer in the defined reaction. The fact that both proteins have been called nucleases does not establish that both must cleave donor nucleic acid during acquisition.
The E. coli E9 mutant phenotype is direct, but a complete loss of its nuclease chemistry is not directly established here; cross-species Cas2 cleavage results must stay separate.

Overexpression acquisition, purified half-site/full-site reactions and captured donor complexes are different endpoints. None alone demonstrates complete naturally regulated immunity, prespacer production, gap filling or all CRISPR subtypes.
Cas2 can have active substrate contacts while contributing noncatalytically to integration; structural contribution does not mean an inert spacer, and contact presence does not guarantee necessity.
modularity_test.verdict: Supports reuse of contributor-attribution reasoning beyond metabolic enzymes, with stronger positive-role evidence from complex/DNA studies. It does not establish a universal Cas2 nuclease-null claim, an automatic episode implementation, or a new slot taxonomy.

record.annotation_consequence: Supports an ATP-hydrolysis-dependent reset contribution in the tested Thermotoga system. Do not equate ATPase capacity with successful coupling or silently generalize across species.

record.starting_question: What does a starvation-induced kinase do when it is dispensable before nitrogen runout?
actual_observations: Ammonium-limited cultures showed yeaG induction. Deletion shortened recovery lag and reduced metabolic heterogeneity yet accelerated viability loss after prolonged starvation; wild-type complementation restored survival. Catalytic-domain variants failed to rescue.
record.annotation_consequence: Adaptation and survival during sustained nitrogen starvation; faster immediate regrowth does not imply improved long-term fitness. Physiological substrate(s) remain unresolved.
record.experiment_dependence: Authors' timed nitrogen depletion, flow cytometry, CFU and complementation; the complete signaling mechanism is not inferred from induction.
record.reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published answer was known during retrieval. Listed experiments and findings are authors' reports; connecting questions and annotation boundaries are our reconstruction unless explicitly identified as authors' rationale.
record.verification_scope: Relevant complete Results subsections on induction/recovery, viability and heterogeneity; culture and CFU methods. No reanalysis of cytometry files.
